Why Sursa walks the long way on cliff walking? Stepping off the cliff costs 100.
Q-learning's target uses the max over next actions, so it ignores the chance that
exploration pushes it off the edge. It learns the optimal edge path,
13 steps, 13. Sursa's target uses the action actually taken,
including epsilon random ones, so sells next to the cliff look dangerous and it
learns a safer path one row up, 17. Neither is wrong, Sursa optimizes the
policy it actually runs, Q-learning the one it would run without
exploration. Limitations that motivate DQN. A Q-table needs one entry port,
state, action. Taxi has 500 states, but Cartpole's state is
four continuous numbers and Atari's is 84 times 84 times 4 pixels.
We need function approximation, Q, SA, theta, which
generalizes across similar states.
